subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub adopt one shared trailing-window popularity contract for publishers, skills, and plugins, and what scoring and publisher-ownership attribution rules should that contract use?
rationale: Current code supplies only partial statistics infrastructure; scoring, ownership transfer, backfill, low-activity behavior, and rollout semantics cannot be safely inferred from existing behavior.

options.title: Adopt Shared Contract
options.body: Define one Weekly and Monthly contract across all three surfaces, record it in specs, and implement the missing backend and UI layers in stages.

options.title: Limit Initial Scope
options.body: Expose periods only on surfaces with complete statistics and explicitly label any narrower entity-specific metric.

options.title: Defer Period Tabs
options.body: Retain the existing all-time browse and seven-day skill-trending paths without adding the proposed cross-surface controls.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Contract
recommendation.body: Define one Weekly and Monthly contract across all three surfaces, record it in specs, and implement the missing backend and UI layers in stages.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available ownership signal is the prior daily-stat and leaderboard schema work central to the proposed contract.
